annotation.title_clean: 無人航空機（ドローン、ラジコン機等）の安全な飛行のためのガイドライン
annotation.title_en: Guidelines for the Safe Flight of Unmanned Aircraft (Drones, Radio-Controlled Aircraft, etc.)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: 国土交通省 航空局 無人航空機安全課 (MLIT, Civil Aviation Bureau)
annotation.venue: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT)
annotation.summary_en: Japan's MLIT guidelines explain Aviation Act rules for unmanned aircraft: definition, registration, pilot licensing and aircraft certification, no-fly zones, flight methods, a three-tier risk category system, safety precautions, insurance recommendations, accident reporting duties, and related laws, for business, hobbyist and parent users.
key_provisions_or_claims: Unmanned aircraft of 100g or more must be registered; pilot licence and aircraft certification systems exist since Dec 2022.
Flight prohibited near airports, in emergency airspace, above 150m, and over densely populated areas without permission.
Flight rules: daytime, visual line of sight, 30m distance from third parties, no dropping objects or carrying hazardous materials.
Risk-based Categories I–III depending on specified flights and third-party access control.
Accidents, injuries, loss of control or fire must be reported to MLIT; insurance and flight plan notification via DIPS recommended or required.
